testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Watch the gauges on your dashboard.
Use your senses to notice changes.
Check important items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: You should check your vehicle regularly while driving. Look at your gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to spot any sign of trouble early.

questions.question: If there is a fire in a cargo trailer, you should:

options.text: Open the trailer doors.
Keep the trailer doors closed.
Cover the trailer with a large, heavy blanket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the trailer doors closed.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors if there is a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes it burn larger and faster.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Usually have a low center of gravity.
Usually have a high center of gravity.
Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.
Cannot be driven on interstate highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually have a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have a high center of gravity and need careful handling. The cargo inside can shift during driving, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Before every lane change.
Only when other vehicles are nearby.
Only when it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every lane change.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before changing lanes. Regular mirror checks should be part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Release your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Turn the wheel back once the vehicle is straight again.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid: First, release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll again. Then steer quickly in the direction you want to go. Finally, turn the wheel back to prevent the vehicle from skidding the other way.

questions.question: If you see a driver who is not paying attention, you should:

options.text: Pass the vehicle quickly.
Stay at a safe distance from the vehicle.
Follow the vehicle closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, keep plenty of space between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: If another driver is following too closely behind you, you should:

options.text: Move into the left lane.
Speed up.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the space between your vehicle and the one in front. This reduces the need for sudden stops and gives the tailgater room to pass. Speeding up is not safe because the tailgater may just follow at the higher speed, creating more danger.

questions.question: Once you stop during the stop/start parking exercise, you should:

options.text: Apply the parking brake.
Keep the vehicle in first gear.
Park at a right angle to the curb.
Block a driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: When parking during the stop/start exercise, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block driveways or intersections.

questions.question: How often should you take a break while driving to avoid fatigue?

options.text: Every half hour.
Every two hours.
Every six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: How does an S-cam brake create friction?

options.text: The brake shoes press against the outside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, what can they do?

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Formally ask you to fix your vehicle's problems.
Call a mechanic for you.
Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a commercial vehicle unsafe, they can remove it from service until it is fixed.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, how often must drivers check that the cargo is secure?

options.text: Every 10 miles.
Every 150 miles.
Every 500 miles.
Every 1,000 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check that your cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every 3 hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Which statement about distracted driving is true?

options.text: It only happens when you are physically distracted, not mentally distracted.
Pre-programming radio stations can increase it.
Eating while driving can help avoid it.
It can be reduced by avoiding complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be reduced by avoiding complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: To reduce distraction, do not have complex or emotionally intense conversations while driving. Pre-programming your radio, avoiding eating and drinking, and not smoking while driving also help. Mental distractions that take your attention away from driving are as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: What happens if you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Other drivers will move to let you turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Reach the center of the intersection before you begin a left turn. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: What type of force must control an emergency brake?

options.text: Mechanical force.
Air pressure.
Gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical force.
questions.explanation: All trucks and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. Air pressure can leak away, so emergency and parking brakes should be controlled by mechanical force.

questions.question: How does vehicle weight affect brakes?

options.text: The heavier the vehicle, the less important brakes become.
The heavier the vehicle, the harder the brakes must work.
The heavier the vehicle, the quieter the brakes sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier the vehicle, the harder the brakes must work.
questions.explanation: Heavier vehicles require brakes to work harder to bring them to a complete stop.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?

options.text: Air pressure.
Mechanical.
Heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency and parking brakes are controlled by mechanical force.

questions.question: What is true about shaded areas of the road?

options.text: They usually do not freeze.
They usually do not have moisture, so they cannot freeze.
They stay icy and slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
They should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay icy and slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer than other parts of the road. Ice in shaded areas stays longer and remains slippery even after ice melts elsewhere.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Quickly and firmly.
Slowly and gradually.
Quickly and then release.
Gradually and then release slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal gradually when stopping. Control the pressure so your vehicle comes to a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Stay the same.
Rise slowly.
Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle's gauges before you drive. After you start the engine, the coolant temperature should rise slowly to the normal operating temperature.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill:

options.text: Use the air brakes.
Shift to a lower gear first, then use brakes to slow down more.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear first, then use brakes to slow down more.
questions.explanation: On a steep hill, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use the brakes only when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Brake while you steer.
Turn more than you need to miss the object.
Turn just enough to miss the object.
Steer and speed up at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just enough to miss the object.
questions.explanation: When turning to avoid an object, turn only as much as needed to clear it. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, you should not:

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Drive into a service station.
Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive into a service station.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, pull off the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and give them your location.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make cargo stand taller in a trailer.
Stop cargo from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload cargo from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing keep cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo to prevent movement. Bracing goes from the top of cargo down to the trailer floor and sides.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share the brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: A maximum safe speed sign means:

options.text: It is a suggestion, and vehicles can go faster.
Only vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds must follow it.
All vehicles must follow it and not go faster.
It only applies to cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles must follow it and not go faster.
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: Looking ahead at the road:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
Is not recommended because it takes your attention away from driving.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead for hazards on the road. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver who doesn't scrape ice off the windshield
Someone driving a rental truck
A driver with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. Examples include drivers with ice on windshields, drivers with items blocking windows, and drivers unfamiliar with a rental truck's limited rear visibility. Simply operating a pick-up truck is not automatically hazardous.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should check all of the following, except:

options.text: That the truck is not overloaded.
That the cargo is balanced.
That the cargo is secured properly.
That the cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.
questions.explanation: When inspecting cargo, check that it is balanced and secured properly. Keep the weight as low as possible to prevent rollovers. Do not overload the trailer.

questions.question: Why should you do routine vehicle inspections?

options.text: Safety.
Good gas mileage.
Comfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safety.
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep you and other drivers safe.

questions.question: What comes out when you drain an air tank?

options.text: Water and oil
Ammonia
Liquid cleaners

questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do before checking the engine compartment?

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
Wheels should be chocked.
The engine should be running.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wheels should be chocked.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine, set the parking brake and/or block the wheels. Check the engine before you get in the cab or start it.

questions.question: How often should you check your cargo when transporting a load?

options.text: Only at the beginning of a drive.
Only after driving a long distance.
After every break.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every break.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and its tie-downs before you start. During your trip, check them within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: What happens when a driver is distracted?

options.text: They usually react well to hazards.
They usually notice things more slowly.
They are usually aware of what is happening around them.
They are usually good to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually notice things more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower thinking, delayed decisions, and wrong actions. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when you can.

questions.question: How does truck weight affect stopping distance?

options.text: It usually has no impact on stopping distance.
It is a major factor affecting stopping distance.
It is not as important as the type of cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major factor affecting stopping distance.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's weight is very important for stopping distance. Heavier vehicles need more brake power to stop completely.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until you are ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake.

options.text: 5 mph
10 mph
15 mph
20 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph
questions.explanation: When going downhill, brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat this as needed.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: The engine oil level.
Removing coolant.
Washing the tire rims.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip engine check, look at the engine oil level, coolant level, and the condition of hoses.

questions.question: If brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does this mean?

options.text: The brakes are working properly.
The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes are new.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you have a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle is against the law.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?

options.text: An explosive.
Liquid.
Corrosive.

questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: The state will notify your employer.
You must tell your employer within two business days.
You must tell your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: If your license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, you must notify your employer within two business days.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: While driving.
When the trailer is straight.
While standing next to the vehicle.
By another person.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting your trip. If your vehicle has a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may squeak.
The brakes may stop working.
The brakes may respond slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: If air pressure gets too low, air brakes may not work. Pressing the brake pedal too often lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: How should a truck be parked?

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.
On the grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Always park so you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for rear tires?

options.text: 1/64 inch
1/32 inch
2/32 inch

questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 inch
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread. Rear tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: Most CDL holders have ____ licenses.

options.text: Excepted
Exempted
Non-excepted
Non-exempted

questions.correctAnswerText: Non-excepted
questions.explanation: Most CDL holders who drive commercial vehicles across state lines are non-excepted interstate commerce drivers.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel during a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: The locking jaws should be open.
The locking jaws should be fully closed around the kingpin.
The locking jaws should be loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws should be fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel locking jaws must be fully closed around the kingpin shaft, not around the kingpin head.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do shortly after?

options.text: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Repair the brakes.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to recheck that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: If you must back up a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing, walk around your vehicle to see the path and check for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely only on them. Use a helper if possible.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: An accident on the road
An open road
A police car helping a driver on the side of the road
An ice cream truck

questions.correctAnswerText: An open road
questions.explanation: Accidents, police cars, and ice cream trucks are all hazards because they can distract drivers or attract children into the road. An open road is not a hazard.
